_about.purpose: Measures ranking quality among candidates who are ALL in the right field. eval_dataset.json only asks 'right field or wrong field', which turns out to be nearly trivially separable; this asks the question a recruiter actually has: given six plausible backend engineers, does the model order them the way a human would?

grading_rubric.5: Exact stack match, senior. The candidate you would interview first.
grading_rubric.4: Exact stack match but thinner: mid-level, or missing part of the infrastructure the posting asks for.
grading_rubric.3: Adjacent stack, strong engineer. Would need to pick up the posting's specific tools.
grading_rubric.2: Right field, junior, partial overlap with the stack.
grading_rubric.1: Right field in name only: different stack, little transferable tooling.

_about.grading_protocol: Grades were assigned from the rubric above by reading each resume against its job posting, before any model score was computed. They were not adjusted afterwards to improve the reported correlation.
_about.known_bias: Two limits, and the second is the one that matters. (1) These are written resumes, not scraped real ones, so they are cleaner and more uniform in length than production input. (2) They were written by the same author who knew how the scorer works. The grades were assigned blind to the model's output, but the resumes themselves were not authored blind to the model's design, so this is not an independent benchmark. It is strong enough to catch a regression and to characterize the failure modes below; it is not strong enough to quote as a production ranking accuracy. Replacing these with resumes the author did not write is the single highest-value improvement available to this project.
observed_failure_modes: No notion of seniority: a junior who names the right tools outranks a senior with an adjacent stack.
Under-ranks transferable experience: a senior Vue engineer places 5th of 6 for a React posting.
Ties inside a tight cluster are ordered arbitrarily: the DevOps top three land within 1.1 points.

jobs.backend_job: Senior Backend Engineer. You will design and operate REST APIs in Node.js and Express backed by PostgreSQL and Redis. Our services are containerized with Docker, orchestrated on Kubernetes, and deployed to AWS through a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline. Strong SQL and a track record owning microservices in production are required.
jobs.frontend_job: Senior Frontend Engineer. Build and own our customer-facing React application in TypeScript, with Redux for state management and Next.js for server rendering. You will work closely with design on a component library, write semantic HTML and maintainable CSS, and care about accessibility and rendering performance.
jobs.datascience_job: Data Scientist. Build and evaluate predictive models in Python using scikit-learn, pandas and numpy. You will own the full modelling loop: feature engineering, cross-validation, hyperparameter tuning and honest model evaluation. Strong SQL for pulling your own training data, and some NLP experience, are both expected.
jobs.devops_job: DevOps Engineer. Own our container platform: Docker images, Kubernetes clusters, and AWS infrastructure. You will build and maintain CI/CD pipelines in Jenkins and GitHub Actions, harden our Linux fleet, and be the person who makes deployments boring. Experience running production databases such as PostgreSQL is a plus.
